disclosures.said: Only the solid coloured boxes that carry a tag are things I am asking about. The thin dashed lines you may see on some pictures are marks left over in the pictures themselves; disregard them.
About screen 24: that picture was taken before the middle of the page had finished drawing; on the running app that middle area shows the same thing as on screen 8.
(there is no 13 and no 29 for you — skip those numbers)

screen1-a1.where: Top right corner, the first of the two pictures next to the 'PDF Reader' title: a small gold crown.
screen1-a1.expectation: I think it would take me to a page asking me to pay for a premium version of the app.
screen1-a1.cue: Only the picture of a crown. There are no words on it.

first_pass.why: A crown is a picture, not a word, and I do not recognise pictures reliably. 'Crown means paid upgrade' is something I have to work out and hold in my head; nothing on this screen confirms it, so I stop and doubt it.
first_pass.solution: Put the word 'Premium' (or 'Upgrade') under the crown.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the crown shows what it is for, and whether the picture would tell you next time
test_cases.action: On the main page, press the crown picture at the top right. Look at what opens (do NOT press "Start Free Trial"). Then close that page with the X at its top left, and look at the crown again.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens does not make clear what the crown is for, or once back you still could not tell from the crown alone next time
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens plainly says what the crown is for, and you would now know the crown without guessing
test_cases.what_happened: On the main page I pressed the gold crown at the top right. After a few seconds a full-screen page opened with a big orange diamond picture and the heading 'Try the Premium plan completely free'. That told me plainly that the crown is about the paid Premium plan. I did not press 'Start Free Trial'. I pressed the X at the top left and was back on the main page, looking at the crown again. The Settings page also shows the crown next to the words 'Upgrade to Premium'. Seeing that twice gives me something to hold on to.

screen1-a1.closing_comment: The offer page says 'Premium' in large words, and Settings shows the crown next to 'Upgrade to Premium', so I think I would remember it now. But I had to press it to find out, which is exactly what I want to avoid. A word under the crown on the main page would remove the guess entirely.

screen1-a2.where: Top right corner, the second picture next to the title: a cog wheel with a spanner across it.
screen1-a2.expectation: I think it opens the app's settings. But the spanner makes me wonder whether it means tools instead.
screen1-a2.cue: Only the picture. The cog suggests settings; the spanner suggests tools, and there is also a 'Tools' tab at the bottom, so the picture points two ways.

first_pass.why: The picture combines two ideas, and there is a separately named 'Tools' button at the bottom. I cannot decide which one this is without pressing it, and I would read the screen over and over trying to settle it.
first_pass.solution: Write 'Settings' under it, and use a plain cog without the spanner so it cannot be confused with 'Tools'.

test_cases.targets: whether the gear-with-spanner is settings or tools, compared with the Tools tab
test_cases.action: On the main page, press the gear-with-spanner picture at the top right and look at what opens. Go back (the arrow at its top left, or the phone's Back key). Then press "Tools" in the bottom bar and look at what opens.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: the gear opens something tools-like, or you still cannot tell the gear and the Tools tab apart
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the gear opens a page plainly named for settings and the Tools tab opens the tools — two clearly different places
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the cog-with-spanner at the top right. A page opened with the title 'Settings' at the top: Keep screen on, Language, Set default reader and so on. I went back and pressed 'Tools' in the bottom bar. That opened a different page of tiles under the headings 'Convert', 'Edit' and 'Manage' (Scan to PDF, OCR, Split PDF...). They are two clearly different places, and the one the cog opens is named 'Settings'.

screen1-a2.closing_comment: The cog opens a page plainly titled 'Settings', and the Tools tab opens a different page of tools, so they are not the same place. My trouble was before pressing: the picture mixes a cog and a spanner, and the answer only came from trying it. A plain cog or the word 'Settings' would settle it.

screen1-a3.where: The row of rounded buttons just under the title, first from the left, the one reading 'PDF'. It is filled in with colour, so it looks like the one currently chosen.
screen1-a3.expectation: I think it would show only my PDF files in the list below. It is already selected.
screen1-a3.cue: The word 'PDF' on it, the row of other file types beside it, and the coloured fill that moves to whichever one is chosen.

first_pass.why: 'PDF' is a file type I know, and the row clearly reads as a choice between file types.

screen1-a4.where: The row of rounded buttons just under the title, second from the left, the one reading 'HWP'. It is white with an outline, so it is not the one chosen now.
screen1-a4.expectation: I think it would show only files of the HWP type. I do not actually know what an HWP file is.
screen1-a4.cue: The word 'HWP', and that its neighbours are file types I know (PDF, Word, Excel, PPT).

first_pass.why: I can infer from the neighbours that it is a kind of document, but 'HWP' itself means nothing to me. I have to reason my way to it rather than simply read it.
first_pass.solution: Spell the type out, for example 'HWP (Hangul document)', or add a short line explaining what it is.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing "HWP" tells you what HWP is
test_cases.action: On the main page, press "HWP" in the row of file types near the top. Look at the whole screen for anything that tells you what HWP is. Then press "PDF" to put it back.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: nothing on the screen tells you what HWP means
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the screen tells you in plain words what HWP files are
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed 'HWP' in the row near the top. It turned blue, the 'Set as default reader' strip reappeared in blue, and the middle of the page still showed the same picture and 'To continue, please allow file access on your device.' with 'Allow Access'. Nothing anywhere on the screen said what an HWP file is. I pressed 'PDF' afterwards and it went back to red.

screen1-a4.closing_comment: Pressing 'HWP' changed colours but told me nothing about what HWP is. I still have to infer it from its neighbours.

screen1-a8.where: Far left end of the grey strip that says 'Set as default reader'. The box holds a very small, faint 'x' at its top corner and the little book picture below it.
screen1-a8.expectation: I think pressing the small 'x' would close this 'Set as default reader' strip. I am not sure whether pressing the book picture does the same.
screen1-a8.cue: A tiny, pale 'x' in the corner. It is so faint I almost missed it.

first_pass.why: The 'x' is the only cue and it is barely visible; the box also covers the book picture, which does not look like a close button at all. I cannot be certain what part I am meant to press or what will happen.
first_pass.solution: Make the close control a clearly visible 'x' of normal size, or a word such as 'Dismiss', on its own, away from the book picture.

test_cases.targets: whether the book picture beside the x does anything different from the x
test_cases.action: On the main page, BEFORE pressing the x, press the small red book picture just right of the x on the grey strip, and see what happens. If the strip is still there afterwards, then press the x itself and see what happens.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: the book and the x do different or surprising things, or you cannot tell which one you pressed
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: pressing that corner simply closes the strip, whichever part you touch
test_cases.what_happened: Right after the app opened, I pressed the small red book picture beside the x on the grey strip, not the x itself. The strip simply disappeared and nothing else happened. Because the strip was gone, there was no x left to press in this test. So the book part and the x part of that corner both just close the strip.

test_cases.targets: whether the small x at the left of the grey strip closes the strip, and nothing else
test_cases.action: On the main page, find the grey strip "Set as default reader". Press the small x at its far left and see what happens. (The strip comes back the next time the app is started.)
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: something opens, nothing happens, or you cannot tell what you pressed
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the strip simply goes away and nothing else happens
test_cases.what_happened: Later the strip came back (after I pressed 'HWP'). I pressed the small x at its far left. The strip went away and nothing opened. The page stayed as it was. It was hard to aim at such a faint, tiny x, but it did exactly what I expected.

screen1-a8.closing_comment: Both the book picture and the x simply close the strip, and nothing else happens. My worry that they might do different things does not hold. The x is still very small and faint, but that is about seeing and hitting it, not about what it does.

test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what appears does not tell you what the button does
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what appears shows plainly what the button does (for example a scanner)

first_pass.why: A crown is a picture, not a word, and I do not recognise pictures reliably. 'Crown means paid upgrade' is something I have to work out and hold in my head; nothing on this screen confirms it, so I stop and doubt it.
first_pass.solution: Put the word 'Premium' (or 'Upgrade') under the crown.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the crown shows what it is for, and whether the picture would tell you next time
test_cases.action: On the main page, press the crown picture at the top right. Look at what opens (do NOT press "Start Free Trial"). Then close that page with the X at its top left, and look at the crown again.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens does not make clear what the crown is for, or once back you still could not tell from the crown alone next time
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens plainly says what the crown is for, and you would now know the crown without guessing
test_cases.what_happened: (run once, on screen1-a1, for every repeat of this control) On the main page I pressed the gold crown at the top right. After a few seconds a full-screen page opened with a big orange diamond picture and the heading 'Try the Premium plan completely free'. That told me plainly that the crown is about the paid Premium plan. I did not press 'Start Free Trial'. I pressed the X at the top left and was back on the main page, looking at the crown again. The Settings page also shows the crown next to the words 'Upgrade to Premium'. Seeing that twice gives me something to hold on to.

screen3-a1.closing_comment: The offer page says 'Premium' in large words, and Settings shows the crown next to 'Upgrade to Premium', so I think I would remember it now. But I had to press it to find out, which is exactly what I want to avoid. A word under the crown on the main page would remove the guess entirely.

screen3-a2.where: Top right corner, the second picture next to the title: a cog wheel with a spanner across it.
screen3-a2.expectation: I think it opens the app's settings. But the spanner makes me wonder whether it means tools instead.
screen3-a2.cue: Only the picture. The cog suggests settings; the spanner suggests tools, and there is also a 'Tools' tab at the bottom, so the picture points two ways.

first_pass.why: The picture combines two ideas, and there is a separately named 'Tools' button at the bottom. I cannot decide which one this is without pressing it, and I would read the screen over and over trying to settle it.
first_pass.solution: Write 'Settings' under it, and use a plain cog without the spanner so it cannot be confused with 'Tools'.

test_cases.targets: whether the gear-with-spanner is settings or tools, compared with the Tools tab
test_cases.action: On the main page, press the gear-with-spanner picture at the top right and look at what opens. Go back (the arrow at its top left, or the phone's Back key). Then press "Tools" in the bottom bar and look at what opens.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: the gear opens something tools-like, or you still cannot tell the gear and the Tools tab apart
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the gear opens a page plainly named for settings and the Tools tab opens the tools — two clearly different places
test_cases.what_happened: (run once, on screen1-a2, for every repeat of this control) I pressed the cog-with-spanner at the top right. A page opened with the title 'Settings' at the top: Keep screen on, Language, Set default reader and so on. I went back and pressed 'Tools' in the bottom bar. That opened a different page of tiles under the headings 'Convert', 'Edit' and 'Manage' (Scan to PDF, OCR, Split PDF...). They are two clearly different places, and the one the cog opens is named 'Settings'.

screen3-a2.closing_comment: The cog opens a page plainly titled 'Settings', and the Tools tab opens a different page of tools, so they are not the same place. My trouble was before pressing: the picture mixes a cog and a spanner, and the answer only came from trying it. A plain cog or the word 'Settings' would settle it.

screen3-a3.where: The row of rounded buttons just under the title, first from the left, the one reading 'PDF'. It is filled in with colour, so it looks like the one currently chosen.
screen3-a3.expectation: I think it would show only my PDF files in the list below. It is already selected.
screen3-a3.cue: The word 'PDF' on it, the row of other file types beside it, and the coloured fill that moves to whichever one is chosen.

first_pass.why: 'PDF' is a file type I know, and the row clearly reads as a choice between file types.

screen3-a4.where: The row of rounded buttons just under the title, second from the left, the one reading 'HWP'. It is white with an outline, so it is not the one chosen now.
screen3-a4.expectation: I think it would show only files of the HWP type. I do not actually know what an HWP file is.
screen3-a4.cue: The word 'HWP', and that its neighbours are file types I know (PDF, Word, Excel, PPT).

first_pass.why: I can infer from the neighbours that it is a kind of document, but 'HWP' itself means nothing to me. I have to reason my way to it rather than simply read it.
first_pass.solution: Spell the type out, for example 'HWP (Hangul document)', or add a short line explaining what it is.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing "HWP" tells you what HWP is
test_cases.action: On the main page, press "HWP" in the row of file types near the top. Look at the whole screen for anything that tells you what HWP is. Then press "PDF" to put it back.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: nothing on the screen tells you what HWP means
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the screen tells you in plain words what HWP files are
test_cases.what_happened: (run once, on screen1-a4, for every repeat of this control) I pressed 'HWP' in the row near the top. It turned blue, the 'Set as default reader' strip reappeared in blue, and the middle of the page still showed the same picture and 'To continue, please allow file access on your device.' with 'Allow Access'. Nothing anywhere on the screen said what an HWP file is. I pressed 'PDF' afterwards and it went back to red.

screen3-a4.closing_comment: Pressing 'HWP' changed colours but told me nothing about what HWP is. I still have to infer it from its neighbours.

screen3-a5.where: The row of rounded buttons just under the title, third from the left, the one reading 'Word'. It is white with an outline, so it is not the one chosen now.
screen3-a5.expectation: I think it would show only my Word files in the list below.
screen3-a5.cue: The word 'Word' on it, the row of other file types beside it, and the coloured fill that moves to whichever one is chosen.

first_pass.why: 'Word' is a file type I know, and the row clearly reads as a choice between file types.

screen3-a6.where: The row of rounded buttons just under the title, fourth from the left, the one reading 'Excel'. It is white with an outline, so it is not the one chosen now.
screen3-a6.expectation: I think it would show only my Excel files in the list below.
screen3-a6.cue: The word 'Excel' on it, the row of other file types beside it, and the coloured fill that moves to whichever one is chosen.

first_pass.why: 'Excel' is a file type I know, and the row clearly reads as a choice between file types.

screen3-a7.where: The row of rounded buttons just under the title, fifth from the left, the one reading 'PPT'. It is white with an outline, so it is not the one chosen now.
screen3-a7.expectation: I think it would show only my PPT files in the list below.
screen3-a7.cue: The word 'PPT' on it, the row of other file types beside it, and the coloured fill that moves to whichever one is chosen.

first_pass.why: 'PPT' is a file type I know, and the row clearly reads as a choice between file types.

screen3-a8.where: Far left end of the grey strip that says 'Set as default reader'. The box holds a very small, faint 'x' at its top corner and the little book picture below it.
screen3-a8.expectation: I think pressing the small 'x' would close this 'Set as default reader' strip. I am not sure whether pressing the book picture does the same.
screen3-a8.cue: A tiny, pale 'x' in the corner. It is so faint I almost missed it.

first_pass.why: The 'x' is the only cue and it is barely visible; the box also covers the book picture, which does not look like a close button at all. I cannot be certain what part I am meant to press or what will happen.
first_pass.solution: Make the close control a clearly visible 'x' of normal size, or a word such as 'Dismiss', on its own, away from the book picture.

test_cases.targets: whether the book picture beside the x does anything different from the x
test_cases.action: On the main page, BEFORE pressing the x, press the small red book picture just right of the x on the grey strip, and see what happens. If the strip is still there afterwards, then press the x itself and see what happens.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: the book and the x do different or surprising things, or you cannot tell which one you pressed
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: pressing that corner simply closes the strip, whichever part you touch
test_cases.what_happened: (run once, on screen1-a8, for every repeat of this control) Right after the app opened, I pressed the small red book picture beside the x on the grey strip, not the x itself. The strip simply disappeared and nothing else happened. Because the strip was gone, there was no x left to press in this test. So the book part and the x part of that corner both just close the strip.

test_cases.targets: whether the small x at the left of the grey strip closes the strip, and nothing else
test_cases.action: On the main page, find the grey strip "Set as default reader". Press the small x at its far left and see what happens. (The strip comes back the next time the app is started.)
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: something opens, nothing happens, or you cannot tell what you pressed
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the strip simply goes away and nothing else happens
test_cases.what_happened: (run once, on screen1-a8, for every repeat of this control) Later the strip came back (after I pressed 'HWP'). I pressed the small x at its far left. The strip went away and nothing opened. The page stayed as it was. It was hard to aim at such a faint, tiny x, but it did exactly what I expected.

screen3-a8.closing_comment: Both the book picture and the x simply close the strip, and nothing else happens. My worry that they might do different things does not hold. The x is still very small and faint, but that is about seeing and hitting it, not about what it does.

screen3-a9.expectation: I think it would make this app the one that opens my PDF files automatically.
screen3-a9.cue: The sentence 'Set as default reader' right beside it.

first_pass.why: The sentence next to it explains the button; in a PDF reader, 'default reader' means the app that opens PDFs.

screen3-a10.where: Middle of the screen, under the sentence 'To continue, please allow file access on your device.': a large black button saying 'Allow Access'.
screen3-a10.expectation: I think it would ask me to give the app permission to see the files on my phone.
screen3-a10.cue: The words 'Allow Access' and the sentence directly above it.

first_pass.why: The sentence tells me what is needed and the button says exactly that. It is large and plain.

screen3-a11.expectation: I think it might open the camera to scan a paper document. That is a guess.
screen3-a11.cue: Only the picture. The corner brackets look like a camera viewfinder. There are no words.

first_pass.why: It is a picture-only button, and I do not recognise pictures easily. I am inferring 'scan' from the shape and could be wrong; it might be a QR-code reader or something else.
first_pass.solution: Put the word 'Scan' on or under the button.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the round black button shows what it does
test_cases.action: On the main page, press the round black button with the corner marks at the bottom right. Look at what appears. Do NOT give any permission: if a box appears, close it with the phone's Back key.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what appears does not tell you what the button does
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what appears shows plainly what the button does (for example a scanner)

screen3-a11.closing_comment: Pressing it only brought up a permission box, so I still do not know whether it is a scanner, a QR reader or something else. The picture alone never told me, and the app did not show me either.

screen3-a12.where: Bottom bar, first of four, a picture with the word 'Home' under it. It is dark and bold, so it looks like the section I am in.
screen3-a12.expectation: It would take me to the main page of the app. I am already on it.

first_pass.why: It has a clear word and a familiar house picture.

screen3-a13.where: Bottom bar, second of four, a picture with the word 'Recent' under it. It is grey, so it is not the section I am in.
screen3-a13.expectation: It would show the files I opened recently.

first_pass.why: The word 'Recent' with a clock tells me plainly.

screen3-a14.where: Bottom bar, third of four, a picture with the word 'Favorite' under it. It is grey, so it is not the section I am in.
screen3-a14.expectation: It would show files I have marked as favourites.

first_pass.why: The word 'Favorite' with a star is plain.

screen3-a15.where: Bottom bar, fourth of four, a picture with the word 'Tools' under it. It is grey, so it is not the section I am in.
screen3-a15.expectation: It would open a page of extra things the app can do with files, such as converting them.

first_pass.why: The word 'Tools' is broad, but as a bottom tab it is a place I can go and come back from with 'Home' right beside it, so I am comfortable pressing it to find out.

screen4-a1.where: Top left corner, over the big orange picture of a diamond: a dark round button with a white 'X'.
screen4-a1.expectation: I think it would close this offer and take me back.
screen4-a1.cue: The 'X', which I know means close.

first_pass.why: An 'X' in a corner is the one close sign I reliably recognise, and it is high-contrast on a dark circle.

screen4-a2.where: Near the bottom: a wide black button saying 'Start Free Trial'.
screen4-a2.expectation: I think it would start a 3-day free trial of the paid plan, and after that I would be charged $29.99 a year unless I cancel.
screen4-a2.cue: The words 'Start Free Trial' and the small line above it, '3 day free trial, then $29.99/year ($2,50/month)'.

first_pass.why: The button itself is plain, but what it commits me to is not. 'Day 2' and 'Day 3' in the timeline say the identical sentence, 'We will remind you when the trial package is about to expire', so I cannot work out when the reminder comes or when the charge starts. I also cannot tell whether pressing it asks for payment now. I would read it over and over.
first_pass.solution: Say on the button or right beside it exactly what happens: 'Free for 3 days. You will be charged $29.99 on <date> unless you cancel.' Give Day 2 and Day 3 different, correct sentences.

test_cases.targets: whether the offer page tells you what "Start Free Trial" commits you to, without pressing it
test_cases.action: On the main page, press the crown at the top right. On the page that opens, read everything around the "Start Free Trial" button — but do NOT press it. Then close the page with the X at its top left.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: the page does not make clear when and how much you would be charged, or you could not find it
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the page says plainly what you commit to and when you would pay
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the crown and read the offer page without pressing anything on it. It says 'Today: Remove intrusive ads, unlock all features, and get high-quality PDF scans.' Then 'Day 2' and 'Day 3' both say exactly the same sentence: 'We will remind you when the trial package is about to expire'. Above the button, in small print, it says '3 day free trial, then $29.99/year ($2,50/month)', and below it, 'Subscription will auto-renew. Cancel anytime.' There is no date for the first charge. Nothing says whether pressing the button asks for payment details now, and the two identical 'Day' lines leave me unsure when the reminder comes. I closed it with the X at the top left.

screen4-a2.closing_comment: Reading everything slowly, I still cannot tell when I would first be charged or whether pressing the button asks for payment now, and 'Day 2' and 'Day 3' repeat the same sentence. I would read this over and over and still not commit.

screen4-a3.where: Very bottom, left: small grey words 'Terms of Use'.
screen4-a3.expectation: I think it would open the terms of use document.

first_pass.why: The words say what it is, although they are very small and faint.

screen4-a4.where: Very bottom, right: small grey words 'Privacy Policy'.
screen4-a4.expectation: I think it would open the privacy policy document.

first_pass.why: The words say what it is, although they are very small and faint.

screen5-a1.where: Across the whole top bar of the page, around the word 'Settings'.
screen5-a1.expectation: I would not expect anything to happen. It looks like the title that tells me I am on the Settings page.
screen5-a1.cue: The word 'Settings', which reads as a page title, not a button.

first_pass.why: As a title it is good; it tells me where I am. But it is boxed as something I could press, and nothing on the screen says what pressing it would do. If it does something, I have no way of knowing what.
first_pass.solution: If it does nothing, that is fine. If it does do something, give it its own clearly labelled button.

test_cases.targets: what pressing the word "Settings" at the top of the settings page does
test_cases.action: On the main page, press the gear picture at the top right to open the settings page. Press once on the word "Settings" at the top (not on the arrow), then wait and take a few screenshots.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: it does something the word "Settings" does not tell you
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: nothing happens — it is only the page title
test_cases.what_happened: I opened Settings with the cog and pressed once on the word 'Settings' at the top, not on the arrow. After a few seconds I was taken out of Settings, back to the main page. To make sure I had not hit the arrow, I opened Settings again and pressed the empty right-hand part of the title bar, well away from both the arrow and the word. Again it took me back to the main page. So the whole title bar works as a back button, and the word 'Settings' does not tell you that.

screen5-a1.closing_comment: Pressing the word 'Settings', or anywhere on that top bar, takes me out of the page. The word gives no hint of that. It is the page's name, and I use the name to know where I am. If I touch it by accident while I am orienting myself, I am suddenly somewhere else. It is worse than I expected, although at least it goes back rather than somewhere new.

screen5-a2.where: Top left corner, next to 'Settings': a left-pointing arrow.
screen5-a2.expectation: I think it would take me back to the previous page.
screen5-a2.cue: The back arrow shape, in the usual place at the top left.

first_pass.why: This is the back button where I expect it, and I rely on it.

screen5-a3.where: Just under the title: a wide orange strip with a crown and the words 'Upgrade to Premium' and an arrow.
screen5-a3.expectation: I think it would open the page about paying for the premium version.

first_pass.why: The words say it plainly. Seeing the crown next to these words also tells me what the crown on the main page probably meant.

screen5-a4.where: First row of the list: a sun picture, the words 'Keep screen on', and a switch on the right (black with the white knob on the right).
screen5-a4.expectation: It is an on/off switch: on means the phone screen will not go dark while I am reading.
screen5-a4.cue: The words 'Keep screen on' and the switch shape.

first_pass.why: I understand what the setting is for. What I cannot tell is whether it is on or off right now: the switch is black, not a colour, and there is no 'On' or 'Off' written. So I do not know whether pressing it will turn it on or turn it off.
first_pass.solution: Write 'On' or 'Off' next to the switch, or use a clear colour for on.

screen5-a5.where: Second row: a language picture, 'Language', and 'English' in blue with an arrow.
screen5-a5.expectation: I think it would open a list where I can change the app's language; it is English now.

first_pass.why: Both the setting and its current value are written out.

screen5-a6.where: Third row: 'Set default reader' with an arrow.
screen5-a6.expectation: I think it would let me make this app the one that opens my documents automatically.

first_pass.why: The words say what it does.

screen5-a7.where: Fourth row: a card picture, 'Add widget', and an arrow.
screen5-a7.expectation: I think it would add a small box for this app to my phone's home screen. I do not know what that box would show or do.

first_pass.why: 'Widget' is a vague word. I know it roughly means something on the home screen, but not what this particular one is, so I cannot decide whether I want it.
first_pass.solution: Say what the widget is, for example 'Add a shortcut to your recent files on your home screen', with a small preview picture.

test_cases.targets: whether "Add widget" shows in ordinary words what it will do before it does anything
test_cases.action: Open the settings page (gear at top right) and press "Add widget". Read what appears. Do NOT press "Add" — close it with the phone's Back key.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what appears does not tell you in ordinary words what you would be adding and where
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what appears tells you plainly what it adds and where, before anything is added
test_cases.what_happened: In Settings I pressed 'Add widget'. A sheet slid up from the bottom with the title 'Add widget', a preview picture of a small panel with a search bar and four buttons (Home, Recent, Bookmarks, Edit PDF), and under it 'PDF Tools – One-tap access to common features'. There was a row of six dots, which I take to mean there are other widget designs to swipe through, and a black 'Add' button. Nothing was added until I pressed Add, and I did not press it. I closed it with Back. The preview shows me what I would get. The words do not say where it goes, although 'widget' plus the picture suggests my phone's home screen.

screen5-a7.closing_comment: The sheet shows a preview and a short line, 'PDF Tools – One-tap access to common features', and nothing is added until I press 'Add'. That is much better than I feared. It still does not say in words where the widget goes, and the six dots mean more choices to page through. The label on the Settings row itself could say what it is.

screen5-a8.where: Fifth row, after a gap: a star, 'Rate App', and an arrow.
screen5-a8.expectation: I think it would take me to the app store to give the app a rating.

first_pass.why: The words say what it does.

screen5-a9.where: Sixth row: a curved arrow, 'Share App', and an arrow.
screen5-a9.expectation: I think it would let me send a link to this app to someone else.

first_pass.why: The words say what it does.

screen5-a10.where: Seventh row, after a gap: 'Privacy Policy' with an arrow.
screen5-a10.expectation: I think it would open the privacy policy.

first_pass.why: The words say what it does.

screen5-a11.where: Last row: 'Terms of Use' with an arrow.
screen5-a11.expectation: I think it would open the terms of use.

first_pass.why: The words say what it does.

test_cases.problem_is_real_if: you could not tell from the button where it would take you, or you are lost once you land
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: it takes you somewhere that the button made clear, and you can tell where you are
test_cases.what_happened: From the Tools page I pressed 'PDF to Image', and the box 'Request permission to access all files' appeared. I pressed 'GO TO SET'. The app handed me over to the phone's own page. It had a large title 'All files access', the app's icon and name 'PDF Reader, PDF Viewer', a switch 'Allow access to manage all files' (off), and a warning that the app could read, modify and delete all files. I touched nothing and pressed Back, which returned me to the Tools page. Once there, I could tell where I was, because the title is large and plain. But 'GO TO SET' had not told me I would leave the app for the phone's settings; I only understood that after landing.

test_cases.targets: whether the permission box offers a way to say no
test_cases.action: Open the same box again (round black button). Look for a way to say no or close it on the box itself; then try the phone's Back key.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: there is no way to decline shown on the box
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: a way to decline or close is shown
test_cases.what_happened: I opened the same box again with the round black button on the main page. The box has only the picture, the title, the paragraph and 'GO TO SET'. There is no 'Not now', 'Cancel' or x anywhere on it. I pressed the phone's Back key and the box closed, leaving me on the main page. I also used Back to close the same box several times from the Tools page, and it worked each time.

screen14-a1.closing_comment: Where 'GO TO SET' takes me turned out to be clear once I arrived: the phone's 'All files access' page with the app's name, and Back brings me straight back. But the button's words did not tell me beforehand that I would leave the app, and the box still shows no way to say no. I only escaped with the phone's Back key, which not everyone would think of.

screen15-a1.where: Top right corner, the first of the two pictures next to the 'PDF Reader' title: a small gold crown.
screen15-a1.expectation: I think it would take me to a page asking me to pay for a premium version of the app.
screen15-a1.cue: Only the picture of a crown. There are no words on it.

first_pass.why: A crown is a picture, not a word, and I do not recognise pictures reliably. 'Crown means paid upgrade' is something I have to work out and hold in my head; nothing on this screen confirms it, so I stop and doubt it.
first_pass.solution: Put the word 'Premium' (or 'Upgrade') under the crown.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the crown shows what it is for, and whether the picture would tell you next time
test_cases.action: On the main page, press the crown picture at the top right. Look at what opens (do NOT press "Start Free Trial"). Then close that page with the X at its top left, and look at the crown again.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens does not make clear what the crown is for, or once back you still could not tell from the crown alone next time
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens plainly says what the crown is for, and you would now know the crown without guessing
test_cases.what_happened: (run once, on screen1-a1, for every repeat of this control) On the main page I pressed the gold crown at the top right. After a few seconds a full-screen page opened with a big orange diamond picture and the heading 'Try the Premium plan completely free'. That told me plainly that the crown is about the paid Premium plan. I did not press 'Start Free Trial'. I pressed the X at the top left and was back on the main page, looking at the crown again. The Settings page also shows the crown next to the words 'Upgrade to Premium'. Seeing that twice gives me something to hold on to.

screen15-a1.closing_comment: The offer page says 'Premium' in large words, and Settings shows the crown next to 'Upgrade to Premium', so I think I would remember it now. But I had to press it to find out, which is exactly what I want to avoid. A word under the crown on the main page would remove the guess entirely.

screen15-a2.where: Top right corner, the second picture next to the title: a cog wheel with a spanner across it.
screen15-a2.expectation: I think it opens the app's settings. But the spanner makes me wonder whether it means tools instead.
screen15-a2.cue: Only the picture. The cog suggests settings; the spanner suggests tools, and there is also a 'Tools' tab at the bottom, so the picture points two ways.

first_pass.why: The picture combines two ideas, and there is a separately named 'Tools' button at the bottom. I cannot decide which one this is without pressing it, and I would read the screen over and over trying to settle it.
first_pass.solution: Write 'Settings' under it, and use a plain cog without the spanner so it cannot be confused with 'Tools'.

test_cases.targets: whether the gear-with-spanner is settings or tools, compared with the Tools tab
test_cases.action: On the main page, press the gear-with-spanner picture at the top right and look at what opens. Go back (the arrow at its top left, or the phone's Back key). Then press "Tools" in the bottom bar and look at what opens.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: the gear opens something tools-like, or you still cannot tell the gear and the Tools tab apart
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the gear opens a page plainly named for settings and the Tools tab opens the tools — two clearly different places
test_cases.what_happened: (run once, on screen1-a2, for every repeat of this control) I pressed the cog-with-spanner at the top right. A page opened with the title 'Settings' at the top: Keep screen on, Language, Set default reader and so on. I went back and pressed 'Tools' in the bottom bar. That opened a different page of tiles under the headings 'Convert', 'Edit' and 'Manage' (Scan to PDF, OCR, Split PDF...). They are two clearly different places, and the one the cog opens is named 'Settings'.

screen15-a2.closing_comment: The cog opens a page plainly titled 'Settings', and the Tools tab opens a different page of tools, so they are not the same place. My trouble was before pressing: the picture mixes a cog and a spanner, and the answer only came from trying it. A plain cog or the word 'Settings' would settle it.

screen15-a3.where: The row of rounded buttons just under the title, first from the left, the one reading 'PDF'. It is filled in with colour, so it looks like the one currently chosen.
screen15-a3.expectation: I think it would show only my PDF files in the list below. It is already selected.
screen15-a3.cue: The word 'PDF' on it, the row of other file types beside it, and the coloured fill that moves to whichever one is chosen.

first_pass.why: 'PDF' is a file type I know, and the row clearly reads as a choice between file types.

screen15-a4.where: The row of rounded buttons just under the title, second from the left, the one reading 'HWP'. It is white with an outline, so it is not the one chosen now.
screen15-a4.expectation: I think it would show only files of the HWP type. I do not actually know what an HWP file is.
screen15-a4.cue: The word 'HWP', and that its neighbours are file types I know (PDF, Word, Excel, PPT).

first_pass.why: I can infer from the neighbours that it is a kind of document, but 'HWP' itself means nothing to me. I have to reason my way to it rather than simply read it.
first_pass.solution: Spell the type out, for example 'HWP (Hangul document)', or add a short line explaining what it is.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing "HWP" tells you what HWP is
test_cases.action: On the main page, press "HWP" in the row of file types near the top. Look at the whole screen for anything that tells you what HWP is. Then press "PDF" to put it back.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: nothing on the screen tells you what HWP means
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the screen tells you in plain words what HWP files are
test_cases.what_happened: (run once, on screen1-a4, for every repeat of this control) I pressed 'HWP' in the row near the top. It turned blue, the 'Set as default reader' strip reappeared in blue, and the middle of the page still showed the same picture and 'To continue, please allow file access on your device.' with 'Allow Access'. Nothing anywhere on the screen said what an HWP file is. I pressed 'PDF' afterwards and it went back to red.

screen15-a4.closing_comment: Pressing 'HWP' changed colours but told me nothing about what HWP is. I still have to infer it from its neighbours.

screen15-a5.where: The row of rounded buttons just under the title, third from the left, the one reading 'Word'. It is white with an outline, so it is not the one chosen now.
screen15-a5.expectation: I think it would show only my Word files in the list below.
screen15-a5.cue: The word 'Word' on it, the row of other file types beside it, and the coloured fill that moves to whichever one is chosen.

first_pass.why: 'Word' is a file type I know, and the row clearly reads as a choice between file types.

screen15-a6.expectation: I think it would show only my Excel files in the list below.
screen15-a6.cue: The word 'Excel' on it, the row of other file types beside it, and the coloured fill that moves to whichever one is chosen.

first_pass.why: 'Excel' is a file type I know, and the row clearly reads as a choice between file types.

screen15-a7.where: The row of rounded buttons just under the title, fifth from the left, the one reading 'PPT'. It is white with an outline, so it is not the one chosen now.
screen15-a7.expectation: I think it would show only my PPT files in the list below.
screen15-a7.cue: The word 'PPT' on it, the row of other file types beside it, and the coloured fill that moves to whichever one is chosen.

first_pass.why: 'PPT' is a file type I know, and the row clearly reads as a choice between file types.

screen15-a8.where: Far left end of the grey strip that says 'Set as default reader'. The box holds a very small, faint 'x' at its top corner and the little book picture below it.
screen15-a8.expectation: I think pressing the small 'x' would close this 'Set as default reader' strip. I am not sure whether pressing the book picture does the same.
screen15-a8.cue: A tiny, pale 'x' in the corner. It is so faint I almost missed it.

first_pass.why: The 'x' is the only cue and it is barely visible; the box also covers the book picture, which does not look like a close button at all. I cannot be certain what part I am meant to press or what will happen.
first_pass.solution: Make the close control a clearly visible 'x' of normal size, or a word such as 'Dismiss', on its own, away from the book picture.

test_cases.targets: whether the book picture beside the x does anything different from the x
test_cases.action: On the main page, BEFORE pressing the x, press the small red book picture just right of the x on the grey strip, and see what happens. If the strip is still there afterwards, then press the x itself and see what happens.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: the book and the x do different or surprising things, or you cannot tell which one you pressed
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: pressing that corner simply closes the strip, whichever part you touch
test_cases.what_happened: (run once, on screen1-a8, for every repeat of this control) Right after the app opened, I pressed the small red book picture beside the x on the grey strip, not the x itself. The strip simply disappeared and nothing else happened. Because the strip was gone, there was no x left to press in this test. So the book part and the x part of that corner both just close the strip.

test_cases.targets: whether the small x at the left of the grey strip closes the strip, and nothing else
test_cases.action: On the main page, find the grey strip "Set as default reader". Press the small x at its far left and see what happens. (The strip comes back the next time the app is started.)
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: something opens, nothing happens, or you cannot tell what you pressed
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the strip simply goes away and nothing else happens
test_cases.what_happened: (run once, on screen1-a8, for every repeat of this control) Later the strip came back (after I pressed 'HWP'). I pressed the small x at its far left. The strip went away and nothing opened. The page stayed as it was. It was hard to aim at such a faint, tiny x, but it did exactly what I expected.

screen15-a8.closing_comment: Both the book picture and the x simply close the strip, and nothing else happens. My worry that they might do different things does not hold. The x is still very small and faint, but that is about seeing and hitting it, not about what it does.

screen15-a9.expectation: I think it would make this app the one that opens my PDF files automatically.
screen15-a9.cue: The sentence 'Set as default reader' right beside it.

first_pass.why: The sentence next to it explains the button; in a PDF reader, 'default reader' means the app that opens PDFs.

screen15-a10.cue: The words 'Allow Access' and the sentence directly above it.

first_pass.why: The sentence tells me what is needed and the button says exactly that. It is large and plain.

first_pass.why: It has a clear word and a familiar house picture.

first_pass.why: The word 'Recent' with a clock tells me plainly.

first_pass.why: The word 'Favorite' with a star is plain.

test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the whole tiles and their names show plainly once the page moves
test_cases.what_happened: On the Tools page I slid the page up once in the middle. The 'Manage' row came fully into view with clear names: 'Import files', 'Print', 'Lock', and a fourth tile I had not seen at all, 'Unlock'. I pressed 'Lock' and got the same permission box, which I closed with Back. Two side effects surprised me. When the page moved, the 'PDF Reader' title with the crown and cog slid away. And when I then pressed 'Home', the main page came back also scrolled, with its title and the crown and cog hidden, until I slid it back down. Before sliding, nothing told me there was more below except that the pictures were cut off.

screen17-a15.closing_comment: Once I slid the page, the Manage tiles showed plain names: 'Import files', 'Print', 'Lock', and an 'Unlock' tile I had not known existed. test_cases.what_happened: (run once, on screen1-a1, for every repeat of this control) On the main page I pressed the gold crown at the top right. After a few seconds a full-screen page opened with a big orange diamond picture and the heading 'Try the Premium plan completely free'. That told me plainly that the crown is about the paid Premium plan. I did not press 'Start Free Trial'. I pressed the X at the top left and was back on the main page, looking at the crown again. The Settings page also shows the crown next to the words 'Upgrade to Premium'. Seeing that twice gives me something to hold on to.

screen34-a1.closing_comment: The offer page says 'Premium' in large words, and Settings shows the crown next to 'Upgrade to Premium', so I think I would remember it now. But I had to press it to find out, which is exactly what I want to avoid. A word under the crown on the main page would remove the guess entirely.

first_pass.why: The picture combines two ideas, and there is a separately named 'Tools' button at the bottom. I cannot decide which one this is without pressing it, and I would read the screen over and over trying to settle it.
first_pass.solution: Write 'Settings' under it, and use a plain cog without the spanner so it cannot be confused with 'Tools'.

test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the gear opens a page plainly named for settings and the Tools tab opens the tools — two clearly different places
test_cases.what_happened: (run once, on screen1-a2, for every repeat of this control) I pressed the cog-with-spanner at the top right. A page opened with the title 'Settings' at the top: Keep screen on, Language, Set default reader and so on. I went back and pressed 'Tools' in the bottom bar. That opened a different page of tiles under the headings 'Convert', 'Edit' and 'Manage' (Scan to PDF, OCR, Split PDF...). They are two clearly different places, and the one the cog opens is named 'Settings'.

screen34-a2.closing_comment: The cog opens a page plainly titled 'Settings', and the Tools tab opens a different page of tools, so they are not the same place. My trouble was before pressing: the picture mixes a cog and a spanner, and the answer only came from trying it. A plain cog or the word 'Settings' would settle it.

screen34-a3.cue: The word 'PDF' on it, the row of other file types beside it, and the coloured fill that moves to whichever one is chosen.

first_pass.solution: Spell the type out, for example 'HWP (Hangul document)', or add a short line explaining what it is.

test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens does not make clear what the crown is for, or once back you still could not tell from the crown alone next time
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens plainly says what the crown is for, and you would now know the crown without guessing
test_cases.what_happened: (run once, on screen1-a1, for every repeat of this control) On the main page I pressed the gold crown at the top right. After a few seconds a full-screen page opened with a big orange diamond picture and the heading 'Try the Premium plan completely free'. That told me plainly that the crown is about the paid Premium plan. I did not press 'Start Free Trial'. I pressed the X at the top left and was back on the main page, looking at the crown again. The Settings page also shows the crown next to the words 'Upgrade to Premium'. Seeing that twice gives me something to hold on to.

screen35-a1.closing_comment: The offer page says 'Premium' in large words, and Settings shows the crown next to 'Upgrade to Premium', so I think I would remember it now. But I had to press it to find out, which is exactly what I want to avoid. A word under the crown on the main page would remove the guess entirely.

screen35-a2.where: Top right corner, the second picture next to the title: a cog wheel with a spanner across it.
screen35-a2.expectation: I think it opens the app's settings. But the spanner makes me wonder whether it means tools instead.
screen35-a2.cue: Only the picture. The cog suggests settings; the spanner suggests tools, and there is also a 'Tools' tab at the bottom, so the picture points two ways.

first_pass.why: The picture combines two ideas, and there is a separately named 'Tools' button at the bottom. I cannot decide which one this is without pressing it, and I would read the screen over and over trying to settle it.
first_pass.solution: Write 'Settings' under it, and use a plain cog without the spanner so it cannot be confused with 'Tools'.

test_cases.targets: whether the gear-with-spanner is settings or tools, compared with the Tools tab
test_cases.action: On the main page, press the gear-with-spanner picture at the top right and look at what opens. Go back (the arrow at its top left, or the phone's Back key). Then press "Tools" in the bottom bar and look at what opens.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: the gear opens something tools-like, or you still cannot tell the gear and the Tools tab apart
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the gear opens a page plainly named for settings and the Tools tab opens the tools — two clearly different places
test_cases.what_happened: (run once, on screen1-a2, for every repeat of this control) I pressed the cog-with-spanner at the top right. A page opened with the title 'Settings' at the top: Keep screen on, Language, Set default reader and so on. I went back and pressed 'Tools' in the bottom bar. That opened a different page of tiles under the headings 'Convert', 'Edit' and 'Manage' (Scan to PDF, OCR, Split PDF...). They are two clearly different places, and the one the cog opens is named 'Settings'.

screen35-a2.closing_comment: The cog opens a page plainly titled 'Settings', and the Tools tab opens a different page of tools, so they are not the same place. My trouble was before pressing: the picture mixes a cog and a spanner, and the answer only came from trying it. A plain cog or the word 'Settings' would settle it.

screen35-a3.where: The row of rounded buttons just under the title, first from the left, the one reading 'PDF'. It is filled in with colour, so it looks like the one currently chosen.
screen35-a3.expectation: I think it would show only my PDF files in the list below. It is already selected.
screen35-a3.cue: The word 'PDF' on it, the row of other file types beside it, and the coloured fill that moves to whichever one is chosen.

first_pass.why: 'PDF' is a file type I know, and the row clearly reads as a choice between file types.

screen35-a4.where: The row of rounded buttons just under the title, second from the left, the one reading 'HWP'. It is white with an outline, so it is not the one chosen now.
screen35-a4.expectation: I think it would show only files of the HWP type. I do not actually know what an HWP file is.
screen35-a4.cue: The word 'HWP', and that its neighbours are file types I know (PDF, Word, Excel, PPT).

first_pass.why: I can infer from the neighbours that it is a kind of document, but 'HWP' itself means nothing to me. I have to reason my way to it rather than simply read it.
first_pass.solution: Spell the type out, for example 'HWP (Hangul document)', or add a short line explaining what it is.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing "HWP" tells you what HWP is
test_cases.action: On the main page, press "HWP" in the row of file types near the top. Look at the whole screen for anything that tells you what HWP is. Then press "PDF" to put it back.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: nothing on the screen tells you what HWP means
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the screen tells you in plain words what HWP files are
test_cases.what_happened: (run once, on screen1-a4, for every repeat of this control) I pressed 'HWP' in the row near the top. It turned blue, the 'Set as default reader' strip reappeared in blue, and the middle of the page still showed the same picture and 'To continue, please allow file access on your device.' with 'Allow Access'. Nothing anywhere on the screen said what an HWP file is. I pressed 'PDF' afterwards and it went back to red.

screen35-a4.closing_comment: Pressing 'HWP' changed colours but told me nothing about what HWP is. I still have to infer it from its neighbours.

screen35-a5.where: The row of rounded buttons just under the title, third from the left, the one reading 'Word'. It is white with an outline, so it is not the one chosen now.
screen35-a5.expectation: I think it would show only my Word files in the list below.
screen35-a5.cue: The word 'Word' on it, the row of other file types beside it, and the coloured fill that moves to whichever one is chosen.

first_pass.why: 'Word' is a file type I know, and the row clearly reads as a choice between file types.

screen35-a6.where: The row of rounded buttons just under the title, fourth from the left, the one reading 'Excel'. It is white with an outline, so it is not the one chosen now.
screen35-a6.expectation: I think it would show only my Excel files in the list below.
screen35-a6.cue: The word 'Excel' on it, the row of other file types beside it, and the coloured fill that moves to whichever one is chosen.

first_pass.why: 'Excel' is a file type I know, and the row clearly reads as a choice between file types.

screen35-a7.where: The row of rounded buttons just under the title, fifth from the left, the one reading 'PPT'. It is white with an outline, so it is not the one chosen now.
screen35-a7.expectation: I think it would show only my PPT files in the list below.
screen35-a7.cue: The word 'PPT' on it, the row of other file types beside it, and the coloured fill that moves to whichever one is chosen.

first_pass.why: 'PPT' is a file type I know, and the row clearly reads as a choice between file types.

screen35-a8.where: Far left end of the grey strip that says 'Set as default reader'. The box holds a very small, faint 'x' at its top corner and the little book picture below it.
screen35-a8.expectation: I think pressing the small 'x' would close this 'Set as default reader' strip. I am not sure whether pressing the book picture does the same.
screen35-a8.cue: A tiny, pale 'x' in the corner. It is so faint I almost missed it.

first_pass.why: The 'x' is the only cue and it is barely visible; the box also covers the book picture, which does not look like a close button at all. I cannot be certain what part I am meant to press or what will happen.
first_pass.solution: Make the close control a clearly visible 'x' of normal size, or a word such as 'Dismiss', on its own, away from the book picture.

test_cases.targets: whether the book picture beside the x does anything different from the x
test_cases.action: On the main page, BEFORE pressing the x, press the small red book picture just right of the x on the grey strip, and see what happens. If the strip is still there afterwards, then press the x itself and see what happens.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: the book and the x do different or surprising things, or you cannot tell which one you pressed
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: pressing that corner simply closes the strip, whichever part you touch
test_cases.what_happened: (run once, on screen1-a8, for every repeat of this control) Right after the app opened, I pressed the small red book picture beside the x on the grey strip, not the x itself. The strip simply disappeared and nothing else happened. Because the strip was gone, there was no x left to press in this test. So the book part and the x part of that corner both just close the strip.

test_cases.targets: whether the small x at the left of the grey strip closes the strip, and nothing else
test_cases.action: On the main page, find the grey strip "Set as default reader". Press the small x at its far left and see what happens. (The strip comes back the next time the app is started.)
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: something opens, nothing happens, or you cannot tell what you pressed
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the strip simply goes away and nothing else happens
test_cases.what_happened: (run once, on screen1-a8, for every repeat of this control) Later the strip came back (after I pressed 'HWP'). I pressed the small x at its far left. The strip went away and nothing opened. The page stayed as it was. It was hard to aim at such a faint, tiny x, but it did exactly what I expected.

screen35-a8.closing_comment: Both the book picture and the x simply close the strip, and nothing else happens. My worry that they might do different things does not hold. The x is still very small and faint, but that is about seeing and hitting it, not about what it does.

screen35-a9.where: Right-hand end of the grey strip reading 'Set as default reader': a red rounded button saying 'SET'.
screen35-a9.expectation: I think it would make this app the one that opens my PDF files automatically.
screen35-a9.cue: The sentence 'Set as default reader' right beside it.

first_pass.why: The sentence next to it explains the button; in a PDF reader, 'default reader' means the app that opens PDFs.

screen35-a10.where: Middle of the screen, under the sentence 'To continue, please allow file access on your device.': a large black button saying 'Allow Access'.
screen35-a10.expectation: I think it would ask me to give the app permission to see the files on my phone.
screen35-a10.cue: The words 'Allow Access' and the sentence directly above it.

first_pass.why: The sentence tells me what is needed and the button says exactly that. It is large and plain.

screen35-a11.where: Bottom right, just above the bottom bar: a round black button with a picture of four corner brackets and a line across the middle.
screen35-a11.expectation: I think it might open the camera to scan a paper document. That is a guess.
screen35-a11.cue: Only the picture. The corner brackets look like a camera viewfinder. There are no words.

first_pass.why: It is a picture-only button, and I do not recognise pictures easily. I am inferring 'scan' from the shape and could be wrong; it might be a QR-code reader or something else.
first_pass.solution: Put the word 'Scan' on or under the button.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the round black button shows what it does
test_cases.action: On the main page, press the round black button with the corner marks at the bottom right. Look at what appears. Do NOT give any permission: if a box appears, close it with the phone's Back key.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what appears does not tell you what the button does
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what appears shows plainly what the button does (for example a scanner)
test_cases.what_happened: (run once, on screen1-a11, for every repeat of this control) I pressed the round black button with the corner marks at the bottom right. No camera or scanner appeared. Instead a white box slid up: 'Request permission to access all files ... please allow "PDF Reader, PDF Viewer" to access all your files.' with one button, 'GO TO SET'. I closed it with the Back key. What appeared did not tell me what the round button itself does; it only asked for permission.

screen35-a11.closing_comment: Pressing it only brought up a permission box, so I still do not know whether it is a scanner, a QR reader or something else. The picture alone never told me, and the app did not show me either.

screen35-a12.where: Bottom bar, first of four, a picture with the word 'Home' under it. It is dark and bold, so it looks like the section I am in.
screen35-a12.expectation: It would take me to the main page of the app. I am already on it.

first_pass.why: It has a clear word and a familiar house picture.

screen35-a13.where: Bottom bar, second of four, a picture with the word 'Recent' under it. It is grey, so it is not the section I am in.
screen35-a13.expectation: It would show the files I opened recently.

first_pass.why: The word 'Recent' with a clock tells me plainly.

screen35-a14.where: Bottom bar, third of four, a picture with the word 'Favorite' under it. It is grey, so it is not the section I am in.
screen35-a14.expectation: It would show files I have marked as favourites.

first_pass.why: The word 'Favorite' with a star is plain.

screen35-a15.where: Bottom bar, fourth of four, a picture with the word 'Tools' under it. It is grey, so it is not the section I am in.
screen35-a15.expectation: It would open a page of extra things the app can do with files, such as converting them.

first_pass.why: The word 'Tools' is broad, but as a bottom tab it is a place I can go and come back from with 'Home' right beside it, so I am comfortable pressing it to find out.
